correctness_confidence.basis: All main theorems, series reductions, Taylor expansions, and asymptotic coefficients were independently verified. The Dirichlet-moment derivation of Theorem 3.1, the parity-binomial reduction of J_q in Theorem 8.2, the MLR dominance in Lemma 8.1, and all five large-q contact expansions (32)-(36) are mathematically sound.

novelty.basis: While orbitope geometry, Gibbs duality, and compact-group symmetrization are classical, the exact complete-homogeneous positive series for the oriented two-plane partition function and the combinatorial one-change theorem via parity-truncated binomial variance and MLR ordering are novel and non-trivial.

reproducibility.basis: All proofs are self-contained and analytic, including an explicit 14th-degree positive polynomial certificate in Appendix A. The supplemental code provides clean, deterministic Python scripts using exact rational arithmetic to verify the finite-dimensional algebra and diagnostic plots.

rigor.basis: The manuscript avoids local Landau approximations or numerical root-finding claims by proving an all-dimension coefficient sign-change theorem (Theorem 8.2) using exact rational bounds and Cauchy's one-change argument, alongside rigorous two-derivative Gamma-tail control for the large-q asymptotics.

significance.basis: Provides a complete, closed-form phase diagram in every dimension n >= 3 for a natural geometric rate-distortion problem on the oriented Grassmannian, establishing a rare exact benchmark for first-order phase coexistence and absence of reentrance in generalized Curie-Weiss-type variational problems.

potential_errors: Minor LaTeX cross-referencing issue (cleveref shared counter): Proposition 11.1, Lemma 8.1, and Lemma 10.1 are rendered as 'theorem 11.1', 'theorem 8.1', and 'theorem 10.1' in the proofs on pages 6, 8, and 11.

In Lemma 10.1 (page 11), the bound on the first and second y-derivatives of L_q(qy)/A_q(y) - 1 is stated concisely in prose; displaying the explicit boundary terms from differentiating the incomplete Gamma integral would make the two-derivative control more transparent.
strengths: Elegant all-field reduction (Theorems 3.1 and 3.2): expanding the Haar Plucker MGF via spherical and Dirichlet moments yields a series in complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials with positive coefficients, immediately proving simple-bivector rigidity at every field strength.

Rigorous global phase classification (Lemma 8.1 and Theorem 8.2): recasting the Cauchy product coefficients of J_q as the variance of a parity-truncated centered binomial distribution and applying monotone-likelihood-ratio ordering plus an explicit rational tail majorant settles uniqueness of the fold and coexistence contact for all n >= 6.
Sharp thermodynamic and high-fidelity asymptotics (Theorem 10.2 and Proposition 11.1): derives exact leading constants and O(log(q)/q) finite-size shifts for all five coexistence observables.

Clear operational scope and precision: carefully distinguishes full-orbitope posterior-mean compression from manifold-constrained quantization and quantum Born-probability models, and explicitly addresses the reducible SO(4) stabilizer in n = 4.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 8.2 (One-change coefficient law for the oriented-plane normalizer): the exact representation of the nonlinear Wronskian-type combination J_q = L_q L'_q - kappa L_q L''_q + kappa (L'_q)^2 in terms of central parity-window binomial moments and its uniform sign-change proof across all dimensions q >= 4.

Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.2: the positive all-degree complete-homogeneous symmetric polynomial series for the Haar oriented two-plane partition function and the resulting all-field simple-bivector extremality.
summary: This manuscript determines the complete Shannon rate-distortion phase diagram of a Haar-distributed oriented two-plane in R^n represented by its signed unit Plucker bivector under squared ambient Euclidean loss, where reconstructions range over the full convex hull (the bivector mass-norm ball). First, by factoring a Haar two-plane via a uniform direction on S^{n-1} and an orthogonal direction on S^{n-2}, the author expands the partition function Z_n(s, B) into a positive series of complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials in the squared canonical skew eigenvalues of B. Because h_k(z) <= (sum z_j)^k with strict inequality at k=2 off the simplex vertices, simple bivectors uniquely maximize the partition function at every fixed norm and field. This reduces the multidimensional variational problem to a 1D overlap density f_n(x) = ((n-2)/2)(1-|x|)^{n-3}. Second, to resolve the global phase diagram for n >= 6, the author proves that the Taylor coefficients of J_q(kappa) = L_q^2(m_q - kappa m'_q) are proportional to r - E[d^2] under a parity-truncated centered binomial law, and uses monotone-likelihood-ratio ordering and an exact rational tail bound to prove a single sign change. This establishes a unique fold, a unique coexistence contact, and no reentrance for all n >= 6, alongside sharp large-n logarithmic contact asymptotics and N-block worst-source capacity tensorization.
weaknesses: The proof of the uniform two-derivative Gamma-tail estimate (Lemma 10.1) is somewhat compressed; writing out the explicit derivative formulas for the positive and negative halves of the beta integral would improve readability.

The operational results in Section 12 (worst-source capacity equality, N-block tensorization, and zero-dispersion strong converse) are fairly direct consequences of compact-group transitivity once the single-letter covariant channel is established, though the author candidly acknowledges this narrow novelty scope in the introduction.
